title: Domain with a Radical in the Denominator
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Find the natural domain of y=1/sqrt(x-5), where the square root sits in the denominator.

steps.title: Merge the Two Restrictions
steps.explanation: The radicand must be nonnegative for the root to exist, and it cannot be zero because the root divides; together this means x-5 must be strictly positive.
steps.why: sqrt(0)=0 in a denominator would still be division by zero, so equality is excluded.

steps.title: Solve the Strict Inequality
steps.explanation: Adding 5 to both sides yields x > 5.
steps.why: Adding a constant preserves strict inequalities.

steps.title: State the Domain
steps.explanation: All inputs strictly greater than 5 work, and the endpoint 5 itself does not.
steps.why: The open parenthesis at 5 records that the function is undefined there.
